title: Read/decode/write-phase exceptions escape _post_one's except tuple, aborting mirror fallback
evidence:
with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=600, context=ctx) as resp:
                body = resp.read()
                if resp.headers.get("Content-Encoding") == "gzip":
                    body = gzip.decompress(body)
            # Overpass reports errors as 200 JSON with a <remark> element
            text = body.decode("utf-8")
            if "<remark>" in text:
                raise RuntimeError(f"Overpass remark: {text[:500]}")
            with open(path, "w") as f:
                f.write(text)
        except (urllib.error.URLError, urllib.error.HTTPError, RuntimeError, TimeoutError) as e:
detail: ConnectionResetError/IncompleteRead during resp.read(), gzip.BadGzipFile, and UnicodeDecodeError are not subclasses of the four caught types, so a transient read failure kills the run instead of trying remaining mirrors.
recommended_fix: Broaden the except to also catch OSError, ValueError, and http.client.HTTPException so fallback to the next OVER_PASS_URLS still runs.

title: Non-atomic cache write + bare exists() cache-hit check: interrupted write permanently poisons the cache
detail: Kill/disk-full/concurrent run during f.write leaves truncated JSON at the final path; every later run reports 'cache hit' then json.load raises JSONDecodeError — no atomic write, no cache validation, no self-heal.
recommended_fix: Write to a temp file then os.replace() into place; optionally validate JSON parses on cache hit before trusting it.

title: Board numbers restated in both tools instead of reading data/balance.json map.* (ODN-5 numbers-single-source)
evidence:
BOARD_W_TILES = 40
BOARD_H_TILES = 30
TILE_PX = 26
--- tools/render_dublin_preview.py:30 ---
TILE_PX = 26          # data/balance.json map.tile_px
detail: balance.json map.* is {w_tiles:40, h_tiles:30, tile_px:26}; neither tool loads or asserts it. If balance.json changes, the bake/preview silently use a stale board fit with no guard.
recommended_fix: Load map.* from data/balance.json in both tools (or assert the constants equal it at startup).

title: --verify on a fresh clone dies with unguarded FileNotFoundError traceback
detail: Cache files are gitignored (.osm-cache/), so after clone they don't exist; --verify (a documented standalone mode) raises FileNotFoundError from open() with no actionable message. Same for a missing --out file.
recommended_fix: Pre-check cache/out existence in verify() and exit with a clear 'run --fetch first / missing output' message.

detail: UTM floats come from pyproj/PROJ; a different version can shift values past the 0.02-tile quantization, making verify() fail across machines. No requirements.txt/pyproject pins the deps anywhere (find returned none).

title: Text file IO without explicit encoding='utf-8' on paths guaranteed to carry non-ASCII (©, —, Dún Laoghaire, OSM tags)
evidence:
with open(path, "w") as f:
                f.write(text)
--- tools/osm_extract.py:532-533 ---
    with open(out_path, "w") as f:
        json.dump(asset, f, separators=(",", ":"))
--- tools/render_dublin_preview.py:176-177 ---
    asset = json.load(open(args.asset))
    palette = json.load(open(args.palette))
detail: All opens use the locale codec; on a non-UTF-8 default (e.g. Windows cp1252) raw cache and asset contain bytes outside it, raising uncaught UnicodeEncodeError/UnicodeDecodeError.
recommended_fix: Pass encoding="utf-8" to every open()/json read/write in both tools.
